briefing.text: The hypothesis is a universal negative: it claims no JAK2-nonmutated MPN patient carries a somatic CALR mutation. It is not a question about frequency, and the known near-mutual-exclusivity of CALR and JAK2 says nothing about whether it holds. Per sample, build JAK2 status and CALR status from data_mutations.txt (Tumor_Sample_Barcode joined to SAMPLE_ID), keep only MPN samples, and count samples that have a CALR mutation and no JAK2 mutation. One credible somatic CALR call in a JAK2-wild-type MPN sample is enough to refute the claim. A count of zero supports it only if those samples were actually profiled for CALR.
briefing.reason: This sets the logic of the decision. Teams often treat it as a frequency or exclusivity question and pick the wrong label.

briefing.text: CALR driver mutations are frameshift indels in exon 9. Type 1 is a 52-bp deletion (p.L367fs*46) and type 2 is a 5-bp TTGTC insertion (p.K385fs*47), and there are many rarer +1 frameshift variants. Exon 9 lies at about chr19:13054500-13055000 on GRCh37. For all Hugo_Symbol==CALR rows, tabulate Variant_Classification, Variant_Type and HGVSp. Do not filter to SNVs or missense calls, or to one protein change, because that misses these mutations. Count every exon 9 frameshift.
briefing.reason: A filter that keeps only SNVs or missense calls makes CALR mutations look absent, which biases the result toward the hypothesis.

briefing.text: Define 'JAK2 mutated' as any JAK2 driver mutation, not just V617F. This includes exon 12 indels around codons 536-547, such as N542-E543del and F537-K539delinsL. Tabulate every JAK2 HGVSp value. Report the result under both definitions (V617F only, and any JAK2 driver), and note whether the conclusion changes.
briefing.reason: The JAK2 definition decides which samples fall in the 'nonmutated' group, so it can move a sample in or out of the counterexample set.

briefing.text: In a minority of MPN patients, CALR mutations occur together with JAK2 V617F, often at low JAK2 burden. A CALR-mutant sample that also has any JAK2 call is not JAK2-nonmutated, so it is not a counterexample. For each CALR-mutant sample, list its JAK2 calls and their VAF (t_alt_count/(t_ref_count+t_alt_count)). Judge the hypothesis only on CALR-mutant samples with no JAK2 call.
briefing.reason: This keeps co-mutated samples from being wrongly counted as counterexamples.

briefing.text: Not every CALR variant is a somatic driver. In-frame exon 9 deletions, silent or intronic variants and changes outside exon 9 may be germline polymorphisms or passengers. For each CALR row, check Variant_Classification, position/exon, Mutation_Status and the somatic or matched-normal fields, including n_alt_count in the normal sample. Base the verdict on somatic exon 9 frameshift calls. Report other CALR variants separately and say whether the conclusion depends on them.
briefing.reason: Counting non-driver or germline CALR variants can create counterexamples that do not exist.

briefing.text: In a cBioPortal MAF, samples with no mutation calls do not appear at all. Take the list of samples from data_clinical_sample.txt and mark a sample JAK2-mutated if it has any JAK2 row in the MAF. Compare how many samples are in the clinical file and how many are in the MAF, and use any profiling or TMB columns to confirm that samples were sequenced.
briefing.reason: Using the clinical file gives the correct denominator and shows whether the sample set was profiled for CALR, which a zero-count conclusion depends on.

briefing.text: Check that Tumor_Sample_Barcode values match SAMPLE_ID, and do not join on PATIENT_ID by mistake. Check for patients with more than one sample: the hypothesis is about patients, so combine each patient's samples before judging. Tabulate CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED/ONCOTREE_CODE and keep only MPN subtypes (PV, ET, PMF, MPN NOS). Non-MPN samples have no bearing on the hypothesis.
briefing.reason: A wrong join, unmerged multi-sample patients or non-MPN samples can assign the wrong JAK2/CALR status and distort the count.

shared_assumptions: Both teams defined 'nonmutated JAK2' solely as the absence of a JAK2 row in data_mutations.txt (exome calls), assuming the exome calls are a complete JAK2 genotype, and did not check it against any study-provided JAK2 annotation.
Both teams assumed that every CALR exon 9 frameshift row is somatic because the sample table says SOMATIC_STATUS=Matched, without checking per-variant normal-sample evidence.
Both treated the whole cohort as a single MPN population and did not ask whether JAK2-nonmutated patients who carry another driver (MPL) still count as 'nonmutated JAK2' under the hypothesis.
unused_evidence: The MAF has a per-sample column 'JAK2/MPL mutation' (values JAK2 / MPL / unmutated). It is constant within each sample and looks like the study's own driver genotype, possibly from a separate assay. At least one sample is labelled JAK2 but has no JAK2 row in the MAF. Neither team's method mentions this column, which is the most direct definition of 'nonmutated JAK2'.

The MAF carries study-specific columns 'Germline reads', 'Germline allele percentage (%)', 'Tumor reads', 'Tumor allele burden (%)' and 'Type of Change'. These can confirm somatic status per CALR row, which team A named as its weakest point, while the standard n_alt_count/Mutation_Status fields are empty.
TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS in the sample table can confirm whether the one clinical sample missing from the MAF was sequenced.
unresolved_weak_points: Team A: per-row somatic status was inferred from study design and canonical alleles, not checked. The germline-read and germline-allele-percentage columns could resolve it, but they were not used.
Team B: assumed no JAK2 mutation went undetected. This was reported, not tested, even though the data hold a study-level JAK2/MPL annotation that can test it directly.
second_readings: 'Nonmutated JAK2' may mean the study's JAK2 genotype (the 'JAK2/MPL mutation' column) rather than 'no JAK2 call in the exome MAF'.

'Nonmutated JAK2' could be read as JAK2-unmutated including MPL-mutated patients, or narrowly as the 'unmutated' (JAK2- and MPL-negative) group. The counterexample count can be reported under both readings.
The claim is about patients, so counts should be per patient, not per sample or per mutation row.
challenge.verdict: I trust the agreed answer fairly well. A universal-negative claim needs only a few credible counterexamples, and both teams found CALR exon 9 frameshifts in JAK2-negative samples. Neither team used the study's own JAK2/MPL genotype column or the germline-read columns, so the definition of JAK2 status and somatic status should be confirmed before release.

questions.question: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: The MAF has a per-sample 'JAK2/MPL mutation' column (JAK2/MPL/unmutated). Cross-tabulate it against your MAF-derived JAK2 status for every sample, and then against CALR status. Does any CALR-mutant sample carry the JAK2 label without a JAK2 row, and does using this column as the JAK2 definition change your counterexample count?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: You named per-row somatic status as your weakest point. For each CALR row, tabulate 'Germline reads', 'Germline allele percentage (%)', 'Tumor reads' and 'Tumor allele burden (%)'. Is any CALR call supported in the normal, and does excluding those calls change the count?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Report the CALR-mutant, JAK2-negative count separately for the 'unmutated' and 'MPL' groups of the JAK2/MPL column, per patient. Does the conclusion hold under both the narrow and the broad reading of 'nonmutated JAK2'?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Your weakest point is undetected JAK2 mutations. The MAF has a per-sample 'JAK2/MPL mutation' column. Cross-tabulate it against your JAK2 calls and against CALR status. Are there discordant samples, and does using this column as the definition of JAK2 status change your count of CALR-positive JAK2-wildtype patients?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: SOMATIC_STATUS=Matched is sample-level. For each CALR call, check the 'Germline reads' / 'Germline allele percentage (%)' columns and the tumour allele burden. Is any CALR call present in the matched normal, and would removing it change the result?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Did you count per patient or per sample? Recount per patient, and report the CALR-mutant JAK2-wildtype patients split by MPL status. Does the label depend on whether MPL-mutated patients count as 'nonmutated JAK2'?

questions.why: Decides whether 'no JAK2 call in the MAF' is a valid definition of JAK2-nonmutated, or whether a separate study-provided genotype should take precedence.

questions.question: Are germline (inherited) frameshift variants in CALR exon 9 reported in the literature, and how do studies tell them apart from somatic CALR driver mutations using matched-normal read counts?
questions.why: Tells us whether the matched-normal read columns must be checked before CALR frameshift calls are accepted as somatic counterexamples.

findings.question: In exome or targeted sequencing studies of myeloproliferative neoplasms, how is JAK2 V617F status usually determined (for example, allele-specific PCR versus sequencing calls), and how often do low-allele-burden JAK2 V617F cases go undetected by exome variant calling?
findings.answer: JAK2 V617F is usually typed by allele-specific quantitative PCR on granulocyte DNA, the most common lab method. In the landmark exome studies (Klampfl 2013; Rumi 2014), JAK2 status came from this separate assay, not from exome calls. Sequencing is less sensitive. In Maslah 2019 (427 patients), the NGS detection limit was about 2% VAF. NGS missed 21 samples that qPCR measured at 0.1-1% burden, plus 1 of 298 at 3%. Concordance was excellent above 2%. Lower-depth exome calling will miss at least as many low-burden cases. I found no figure specific to exome calling. 'No JAK2 call in the MAF' is therefore only a weak proxy for JAK2-nonmutated. A study-provided JAK2 genotype or clinical column should take precedence when one exists.
findings.confidence: high for the method and NGS sensitivity limits; medium for how this carries over to exome calling

In the landmark exome studies (Klampfl 2013; Rumi 2014), JAK2 status came from this separate assay, not from exome calls. Sequencing is less sensitive. In Maslah 2019 (427 patients), the NGS detection limit was about 2% VAF. NGS missed 21 samples that qPCR measured at 0.1-1% burden, plus 1 of 298 at 3%. Concordance was excellent above 2%. Lower-depth exome calling will miss at least as many low-burden cases. I found no figure specific to exome calling. 'No JAK2 call in the MAF' is therefore only a weak proxy for JAK2-nonmutated. A study-provided JAK2 genotype or clinical column should take precedence when one exists. HOW SURE: high for the method and NGS sensitivity limits; medium for how this carries over to exome calling. SOURCES: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30259120/, https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1311347, https://doi.org/10.1182/blood-2014-01-550434.

findings.question: Are germline (inherited) frameshift variants in CALR exon 9 reported in the literature, and how do studies tell them apart from somatic CALR driver mutations using matched-normal read counts?
findings.answer: In the sources I read, germline CALR exon 9 variants are in-frame deletions in multiples of 3 bp, clustered near codons 393-405 (e.g. p.Glu405del, p393_395del). They are rare and of uncertain significance. I found no report of a germline +1 frameshift. All 36 frameshift types in Klampfl 2013 were somatic. In familial MPN, every CALR indel was present in granulocytes but absent from T lymphocytes (Rumi 2014). Studies establish somatic versus germline status by testing a matched normal (T cells or buccal cells). Germline variants appear at about 50% VAF in both the tumour and the normal sample; somatic drivers are absent from the normal. Practical implication: a CALR exon 9 frameshift in the MAF is almost certainly somatic, and checking matched-normal read counts is a sensible sanity check rather than a necessity. In-frame CALR exon 9 deletions should not count as driver counterexamples. The web does not rule out an isolated germline frameshift case report that I did not find.
